name: Kurudu
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Anceaux, J.C. 1961. The Linguistic Situation in the Islands of Yapen, Kurudu, Nau and Miosnum, New Guinea. KITLV Verhandelingen 35. Not found online.

sources.citation: van den Heuvel, Wilco. 2025. 'Phonology, main issues' work document (kjr0138) for bundle 'Phonology, final =a on verbs and in clauses', ELAR deposit 0791. 8 pp.
sources.note: Lists 'Waar ligt de stress?' (where does the stress lie?) as an open question to note per verb form; no answer or generalisation given.

sources.citation: ELAR bundle kjr0135 'Demonstratives and stress / Demonstratif dan penekanan' (van den Heuvel & Rumaikewi, 2024-07-19), deposit 0791.
sources.note: Metadata only: two untranscribed recording sessions probing the stress pattern of short demonstrative clitics vs longer forms. Audio/video, no written analysis.

sources.citation: van den Heuvel, Wilco (researcher) & Stevanus Rumaikewi (speaker). 2024-2025. ELAN transcripts kjr0132_01/_02, bundle 'On the search for lexical stress / Pencarian stres leksikal', ELAR deposit 0791 (created 2024-07-05).
sources.note: Bundle description: sessions 'to get a better grasp of potential lexical or phrasal stress'. IPA tier marks prominence mostly on the penult of the lexical word (si'ne, so're, re'vo, i'vo, ki:'ro, ni:'ro, sya'ra, ri'ro, ka'ti, a'pi, i'ta; but a'na, o'pua~opu'a). Researcher notes: 'The stress in the ipa does not correspond to loudness. Possibly height and length; further research needed'; 'Again rather long penultimate niro'; 'Hard to hear the precise location of stress'. Raw field notes, not a statement.

sources.citation: Kamholz, David. 2014. Austronesians in Papua: Diversification and change in South Halmahera-West New Guinea. PhD dissertation, UC Berkeley.
sources.note: Kurudu data second-hand (Anceaux 1961, Silzer 1983, ACD); Kurudu and Wabo called 'unavoidable exceptions' to coverage. Sec. 5.4: penultimate stress reconstructed for Proto-SHWNG from Buli, Sawai, Taba, Ambai, Wandamen, Waropen, Warembori; Kurudu not among languages with a stress description. p. 38 reports Price & Donohue (2008 ms): 'other languages of Yapen also have complex stress systems' (no Kurudu specifics).

sources.citation: Masoka, Ayub, Stevanus Rumaikewi & Wilco van den Heuvel (comp.). 2025. Ro Kruidu: Teks, kamus dan tatabahasa [Booklet with Kurudu texts, lexicon and grammar], bundle kjr0131 in van den Heuvel & Schapper, Documentation of Kurudu (ELAR deposit 0791, ELDP SG1022). 72 pp.
sources.note: Orthography note pp. 4-6 (v vs w, no f); texts, wordlists, phrases. No mention of stress/tekanan anywhere.

sources.citation: van den Heuvel, Wilco. 2025. Metadocumentation for deposit 0791 (Kurudu), ELAR. 7 pp.
sources.note: Orthographic conventions (phonemic transcription, IPA-based; {g},{ng},{v},{y}); nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Gasser, Emily. 2024. Contact, inheritance, and the lexicon of Proto-Yapen. Slides, 16-ICAL.
sources.note: Kurudu forms cited without stress marks; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Masoka, Ayub & Yusup Rumbindi. 2021. Handwritten Kurudu wordlist and phrases (Mnusndu, 21-01-2021), ELAR bundle kjr0122 'Wordlist and grammar by Ayub Masoka and Yusup Rumbindi'. 49 pp. scan.
sources.note: Greetings/phrases/wordlist only (scanned-checked pp. 2-4; same material typed in kjr0131 pp. 54-72). Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Gasser, Emily. 2017. Papuan-Austronesian language contact on Yapen Island: a preliminary account. NUSA 62: 101-155.
sources.note: Kurudu lexical data from 'Anceaux (1992); Xavier Bach (p.c.)'; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Rumbewas, Oni (ed.). 2014. Menyelamatkan bahasa Kurudu, Seri 1 (Buletin Intoren). Makassar: PT Adi Perkasa. 40 pp. scan in ELAR bundle kjr0123 (Glottolog ref 685555).
sources.note: Bible-based Kurudu reading texts for the Jayapura congregation (scanned-checked front matter and TOC pp. 2-5); no phonology, nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Price, David S. & Mark Donohue. 2009. Report on the Ansus survey, West Yapen Island. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2009-001.
sources.note: Kurudu only in classification remarks (East Yapen with Wabo); nothing on Kurudu stress.

sources.citation: Silzer, Peter J. 1983. Ambai: an Austronesian language of Irian Jaya, Indonesia. PhD thesis, ANU.
sources.note: Kurudu only in lexicostatistics and Appendix A pronoun/subject-prefix comparison; no Kurudu stress statement.

sources.citation: Anceaux, J.C. 1961. The linguistic situation in the islands of Yapen, Kurudu, Nau and Miosnum, New Guinea. Verhandelingen KITLV 35. 's-Gravenhage: Nijhoff. (OAPEN/archive.org scan, DOI 10.26530/oapen_613371)
sources.note: Kurudu = section P p. 12 (dialects Kurudu/Kaipuri, ~1100 speakers, Biak influence); Kurudu forms passim in comparative wordlist. p. 14: 'Stress-accent, vowel pitch and vowel length (part of the accentual system in many of these languages) are not indicated.' Only accent remark in the book is Papuma (p. 7). Nothing on Kurudu stress.

sources.citation: van den Heuvel, Wilco (& Antoinette Schapper). forthcoming. Grammar sketch / phonology of Kurudu arising from ELDP SG1022 'Documentation of Kurudu' (fieldwork 2023-2025); incl. analysis of bundles kjr0132 'On the search for lexical stress' and kjr0135 'Demonstratives and stress'.

sources.note: Only modern first-hand phonological work on Kurudu; the depositor is actively investigating lexical stress (dedicated elicitation bundles) and a write-up would give the first explicit statement. Worth contacting the depositor.
